title: edge-hosting-journey-matrix-and-poc-plan
content:
Purpose: quick, workshop-friendly matrix + pragmatic POC plan to help mid-market customers decide between Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private paths, with an explicit migration journey and fallbacks. This is intentionally conversational — meant for SE workshop handoff and prep.

Summary takeaways (TL;DR):
- Start hosted to validate product/ML quality quickly; measure latency percentiles and token cost.
- Move to Dedicated when predictable throughput, SLA, and data isolation justify reserved commit.
- Private is for strict residency/regulatory customers; treat as a separate engagement with ops + security prep.
- Key lever differences: SLA, operator burden, TCO profile, data residency, upgrade cadence, rollback complexity.

Decision matrix (rough scoring; 1=weak, 5=strong):
Criteria | Hosted | Dedicated | Private
------------------------------------------------------------
Time-to-implement | 5 | 3 | 1
SLA/Control | 2 | 4 | 5
Data residency / sovereignty | 2 | 3 | 5
Operational burden (customer) | 1 | 2 | 5
Cost elasticity | 5 | 3 | 2
Predictable throughput | 2 | 5 | 5
Security integrations (KMS/HSM) | 2 | 3 | 5
Custom kernel/quantization ops | 1 | 4 | 5
Observability parity | 4 | 4 | 3
Total (qual) | 24 | 32 | 36

Notes on the scoring: these are engineer-facing shorthand. Customers often trade off Time-to-implement vs Control. Dedicated is often the sweet spot for SaaS customers scaling to thousands of RPS who still want Redwood-managed infra but with reserved capacity.

Customer archetype vignettes (use in workshop):
1) Early-stage AI SaaS (fast iteration): wants speed, low friction, uncertain traffic pattern. Recommendation: Hosted proof-of-value for 6–8 weeks. Success metrics: integration in <2 weeks, median gen latency <150ms for common path, monthly token cost < $X (customer-specific).
2) Retail analytics platform (predictable peaks): needs predictable throughput, regional fallbacks, some PII. Recommendation: Dedicated with tenant-slicing + regional fallback. Success metrics: sustained 99th percentile latency SLA under commit during promotion window; cold-start tail <2x median.
3) Regulated financial customer: strict residency, audit controls, HSM. Recommendation: Private deployment with on-prem gateway or VPC private control plane. Success metrics: SOC2 evidence, key rotation flow documented, successful end-to-end runbook dry-run.

Workshop agenda (90 minutes):
- 0–10m: Goals and pain; customer personas and constraints (privacy, latency, budget).
- 10–25m: Walk the decision matrix; collect which criteria matter most for them.
- 25–45m: Live scenario mapping: show which endpoints fall in Hosted/Dedicated/Private and why.
- 45–70m: POC plan options (quick hosted demo, 4-week Dedicated pilot, 12-week Private onboarding).
- 70–85m: Risks, rollback plans, and E2E success metrics.
- 85–90m: Action items and next steps.

POC plan templates (pick one depending on outcome):
A) Hosted quick validation (2–6 weeks)
  - Goals: validate model quality, basic latency, product integration.
  - Scope: 1–3 endpoints, synthetic traffic mix + 1 week of production shadow.
  - Deliverables: perf dashboard, cost estimate, token-level breakdown, request tracing sample.
  - Quick checks: function calling + tool integration, streaming behavior, rate-limit profile.
  - Exit criteria: integration deployed, sample of 1k real requests with errors <2%, business owner sign-off.

B) Dedicated pilot (6–12 weeks)
  - Goals: validate sustained throughput and autoscale behavior under expected peak.
  - Scope: reserved pool sizing (heatmap-based), routing policy tests, canary rollback on model variant.
  - Infra reqs: VLAN peering options, private subnet plans if using private connectivity, test keys.
  - Deliverables: SLA statement template, cost model across commit sizes, autoscale tuning notes.
  - Exit criteria: achieve latency SLOs under commit, cost within 10% of model forecast, ops runbook baked.

C) Private onboarding (12–20+ weeks)
  - Goals: full parity with Hosted API while meeting compliance and network controls.
  - Scope: VPC/private control plane, KMS/HSM integration, audit logging, baseline observability export, runbook for upgrades.
  - Pre-reqs: legal/compliance checklist, network topology diagrams, root & intermediate certs, firewall rules, secrets management plan.
  - Deliverables: signed acceptance, DR/rollback runbook, playbook for model upgrades and emergency fallback to Redwood-hosted (optional).
  - Exit criteria: successful DR test, audit log validation, security sign-off.

Tradeoffs and non-obvious items (notes to self):
- Caching semantics: prefix/KV caches improve TCO but can complicate multi-tenant isolation. For Dedicated suggest per-tenant KV namespaces.
- Quantization and custom kernels: Private allows deepest customizations but increases upgrade friction. Document a compatibility matrix for each model family.
- Observability: we often see customers equate "more dashboards" with readiness; push an SLI-focused subset (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, token/sec, cost per 1000 tokens).
- Fallback routing: explicit plan for model parity when falling back from Private->Hosted to avoid behavior drift (model variant mapping table).

Open questions for engineering follow-up:
- Can we automate a "private->hosted fallback" config generator that maps endpoint and prompts to safe hosted model variants? (JIRA: SE-3481)
- What minimum KMS/HSM features do we require for Private v1 (key rotation, HSM-backed signing)? Tag to security team.
- Does Dedicated support customer-side VPC peering in the APAC region yet? Need infra confirmation.

Risk register (short):
- Data residency misconfig (medium) => Mitigation: pre-engage legal + network runbook + sample SFTP transfer test.
- Unexpected tail latency under load (high) => Mitigation: workload-aware batching + warm pool testing.
- Cost unexpectedly high in Hosted during POC (medium) => Mitigation: token caps + throttles + real-time cost alerts.

Suggested artifacts to hand customer after workshop:
- One-pager: recommended path + 90-day roll plan (customized).
- Tableau/CSV: synthetic run metrics and cost projection table.
- Runbook: minimal ops playbook for canary rollback.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Marco Ruiz: produce Dedicated commit cost simulation (spreadsheet) — ETA 2024-09-26.
- Aisha Patel: security checklist for Private (KMS/HSM baseline) — ETA 2024-10-03.
- Leah Morgan: create workshop slide deck and persona handouts — ETA 2024-09-18.
- Evan Chen: confirm APAC VPC peering support with infra — ETA 2024-09-20.

Appendix: quick sample cost-projection columns to include in spreadsheet: monthly-commit-GPU-hours, average-token-rate, 95th-percentile-latency, cache-hit-rate, estimated-monthly-cost, per-inference-cost, margin-vs-hosted.

Quick notes to presenter: be explicit about what "control" really buys the customer — sometimes a promise of "we can put it in your VPC" doesn't address model drift or audit evidence. Emphasize measurable success criteria early.

Unresolved scratch items (for internal):
- Determine canonical list of model-variant aliases (map between hosted model ids and private images).
- Template legal language for Private pilot scope of responsibility.

End.
